title: Social Justice PIL — Vulnerable Classes, Dignity and Access

content.overview: Social-justice PIL uses liberalised standing and flexible process under Articles 32 and 226 to enforce fundamental rights and public duties for vulnerable classes — bonded labour, custodial conditions, basic dignity — subject to bona fides and abuse filters.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Vulnerable class and concrete injury? (2) Art 21/14 or statutory duty? (3) Access barrier? (4) Bona fides? (5) Implementable relief?
content.study:
Core idea: PIL’s philosophy is access to justice for those who cannot reach the court. Social-justice claims typically combine Article 21 (and related rights), representative standing, and sometimes continuing directions.

Not a free policy charter: Relief must tie to legal rights and duties. Private disputes and vague governance prayers fail.

Current-law framing: Articles 21, 14, 32, 226; standing and limits topics. Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Vulnerable classes and access
sections.body: Persons without means, literacy, or freedom of movement are the classic beneficiaries of social-justice PIL.

sections.heading: Rights and duties base
sections.body: Article 21 dignity/liberty claims, equality claims, and statutory public duties supply the justiciable frame.

sections.heading: Standing and process
sections.body: Representative standing and, where fit, epistolary initiation and continuing mandamus serve effective enforcement.

sections.heading: Relief design
sections.body: Directions should be implementable and tied to the duty; monitoring may follow continuing default.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: Abuse filters and self-restraint against running administration still apply.

examples.title: Bonded labour class claim
examples.body: Representative petition for release and rehabilitation under Article 21 with possible continuing directions.

examples.title: Private service claim as social justice
examples.body: Individual transfer dispute labelled social-justice PIL — private-dispute filter applies.

hypotheticals.question: Is every poverty-related grievance maintainable PIL?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. There must be a justiciable right or duty, class/public character, and bona fides.

distinctions.title: Social-justice PIL vs private grievance
distinctions.left: Class/public rights enforcement for the vulnerable.

misconceptions.trap: Social justice means courts must grant any welfare prayer.
misconceptions.correction: Relief remains tied to legal rights and duties under 32/226.
